assertions.evidence: One Critical finding; reserve and increment_view_counter are the same read-then-write shape.
Graded Critical: a lost reservation is silent data corruption — the store believes the stock is reserved and the customer believes it is theirs.
Reported under Correctness / Data (A3) on the isolation rule, not under A2 — no threads are involved; the interleaving is between transactions.

assertions.text: Identifies the separate SELECT and UPDATE in reserve with no lock and no atomic operator
assertions.evidence: Cites lost_update_race.py:22-31 — a SELECT followed by an UPDATE on the same row inside one connection but not one atomic statement.

assertions.text: Notes the default isolation level permits an interleaving between the read and the write
assertions.evidence: Cites the file's own DEFAULT_ISOLATION constant at line 8 and the absence of any isolation raise or lock.

assertions.text: Identifies increment_view_counter as the same read-then-write shape
assertions.evidence: Cites lines 35-41 — the counter is written back from a value read two statements earlier.

assertions.text: Failure scenario names oversold stock with no row recording the lost update
assertions.evidence: States both reservations commit, only one is persisted, and nothing in the schema or the logs records the shortfall.

assertions.text: Fix recommends a conditional atomic UPDATE or SELECT FOR UPDATE
assertions.evidence: Fix: a single UPDATE ... SET available = available - qty WHERE sku = ? AND available >= qty, checking the affected-row count; or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before the write.
